title: Experience Is the Human LoRA: A Readout-Retention Theory of Selective Model Change
note: Master Equation River v1.4 credits Human LoRA (citep{human_lora}) conceptually for the selective-retention idea (Src tags on master eq.8, and the master's own eq.(lowrank)/eq.(gate) inherit its intent), but no symbol from this paper's own formalism (O_H, Delta O, B_nA_n, rank_Q, m_n/d_n, the finite-bottleneck postulate) appears anywhere in master-river/v1_4/main.tex -- the master river restates the retention idea in Experience-Is-Meaning-Giving's own U_H(...) notation instead, and states explicitly that eq.(lowrank)-eq.(gate) 'are not v8.1's own text' and are Master's own proposal inheriting from an undeposited Fusion draft, not from this paper. Every equation below is therefore mapped to null: cited-for-idea is not restated-verbatim.

equations.meaning: Definition 1: a finite experience event tuple, making transformation internal to the event arc rather than a later external process.
A genuine experience implies at least one finite state difference at the event scale, even when the durable component later decays to zero.
The phenomenal (first-person) description of a Human LoRA event.
The adaptive (third-person) description of a Human LoRA event.
The central identity thesis: the lived appearance and the adaptive reorganization belong to the same finite event (token-level, dual-aspect identity, not Pn = DeltaOn as mathematical objects).
The active event-level update, factored through the active readout field.

equations.text: g_n = Gamma_n(s_n, r_n^err, q_n, v_n, c_n, p_n) in Q intersect [0,1]
equations.meaning: The retention gate, a function of salience, finite residual, repetition/retrieval, value relevance, context fit, and replay/practice.
The durable update: the retention gate scales the fast/transient update.
The next-step organization update, with epsilon_n the disclosed remainder not captured by the factorized adapter.
The Human Finite-Bottleneck Postulate: the active experience field is strictly smaller than the operational organization it can modify (an explicit open empirical premise).

equations.text: A_n in Q^{m_n x d_n},  B_n in Q^{d_n x m_n}
equations.meaning: The two factor matrices mapping current organization into active event coordinates and back into future organization.
The event-level operator update as a matrix product of the two factors.
Finite factorization rank bound (ThQ, proved in-article): under m_n < d_n the event update cannot have full rank in the operational space.

equations.text: (O_H[n] + B_n A_n) x = O_H[n] x   whenever A_n x = 0
equations.meaning: Selective preservation (ThQ): directions not admitted into the active event channel remain unchanged by that event-level adapter.

equations.text: rank_Q( sum_{i=1}^{N} Delta O_i ) <= sum_{i=1}^{N} m_i
equations.meaning: Composition bound (ThQ): the rank of N summed finite event updates is bounded by the sum of their individual rank bounds.

equations.text: O_H[N] = O_H[0] + sum_{n=0}^{N-1} g_n B_n A_n + sum_{0<=i<j<N} Lambda_{ij} + sum_{n=0}^{N-1} epsilon_n
equations.meaning: Transformative experience as composed Human LoRA: many low-rank event updates plus their pairwise interaction terms Lambda_ij plus remainders can jointly reorganize the base organization.
An intentional episode selecting an object node x and an aspect node y within the active relational graph.
The horizon represented as a finite active neighbourhood of currently co-available/implied distinctions.

equations.text: Delta O^{old}_{new} = g_n B_n A_n Q_n(Delta O^{old})
equations.meaning: Discrete form of retrieval-mediated reconsolidation: retrieval reactivates part of an earlier adapter inside a new event field via a finite retrieval map Q_n.
